questions.q: In the Harborline case study, what does the approval process's entry criteria check?
options: Status = "Submitted" AND Discount_Percent__c > 10
Status = "Approved" AND Discount_Percent__c > 10
Any quote regardless of discount amount
Only quotes created by a sales manager
questions.explain: A quote under a 10% discount never enters the process at all -- the entry criteria is the first filter.

questions.q: Why does a 12% discount never reach the Sales Director's approval queue?
options: The Sales Director opted out of the process
The two-step design routes it to the owner's manager instead, reserving the director for discounts over 25%
12% discounts are automatically rejected
Discounts under 15% skip approval entirely
questions.explain: Tiering approvers by severity means only deals large enough to justify senior attention reach the second step.

questions.q: Why does the quote record lock while the approval is pending?
options: Locking is required by Salesforce for all approval processes
It hides the record from the approver
It prevents the rep from editing the discount while the manager is reviewing the original number
It automatically rejects the quote after 24 hours
questions.explain: Without locking, the approver could be reviewing numbers that no longer match the record.

questions.q: What was the actual business problem at Harborline before any Salesforce design began?
options: A missing Salesforce license
Too many Salesforce users
A broken validation rule
Stalled deals, unchecked large discounts, and no audit trail for who approved what
questions.explain: The three original complaints were business complaints, not configuration problems -- translating them into requirements came first.

questions.q: Where does the record of each approval or rejection decision end up, with no extra data entry required?
options: The quote's own Approval History related list
A separate spreadsheet finance maintains manually
An email inbox
It is not recorded anywhere by default
questions.explain: Approval History logs every step automatically, which is exactly the audit trail the original complaint was missing.
